hero.title: # Study Law in France for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: France is an attractive destination for students interested in study law, international relations, public policy, business law and human rights. Its universities offer established legal education programmes that explore the French legal system, European Union law and international legal frameworks.

overview: France is an attractive destination for students interested in study law, international relations, public policy, business law and human rights. Its universities offer established legal education programmes that explore the French legal system, European Union law and international legal frameworks.
Studying in France offers Indian students access to world-class public universities, prestigious Grandes Écoles, highly subsidized European tuition fees, and rich cultural heritage.

Edu Hawk Worldwide Consultancy guides Indian students through Campus France procedures, English-taught and French-taught university selection, Etudes en France portal registration, France student visa requirements, and post-study work pathways.

universities.name: Important points to check include
universities.desc: Whether the institution is authorised to award the stated qualification. Whether the programme leads to a recognised national degree or an institutional diploma. Whether the qualification carries the expected academic credits. Whether the degree meets admission requirements for further study. Whether the qualification is accepted by the professional regulator in the country where the student intends to work. The French Licence and Master structure is organised within the European higher education framework, but individual programmes can have different awards and requirements. ### Professional Recognition and Legal Practice Professional recognition is separate from academic recognition. Completing a law degree does not automatically grant the right to practise as an avocat (lawyer) in France. The professional route includes additional eligibility and training requirements. Applicants should consult official French guidance on access to the legal profession. Students intending to return to India or another country should check local rules for legal practice, foreign degree recognition and any required examinations or additional qualifications. ## 9. Salary and Job Opportunities After Studying Law in France A law degree from France can support careers in legal services, business, public administration, policy, research and compliance. Available roles depend on the degree, language proficiency, experience, work authorisation and professional licensing requirements. Potential career paths include: Legal Researcher Corporate Legal Assistant Compliance Analyst Contract Management Specialist Data Protection or Privacy Analyst Legal Operations Professional International Relations or Policy Analyst Human Rights Programme Officer Legal Academic or Research Associate Lawyer or Legal Adviser, after meeting the applicable professional requirements ### Salary Expectations There is no single salary range that applies to all law graduates in France. Pay differs significantly between entry-level support roles, in-house legal positions, compliance careers, specialist legal roles and qualified lawyers. Salary is influenced by factors such as: Employer and industry. Location and cost of living. French-language proficiency. Relevant internships and professional experience. Specialisation and additional qualifications. Professional registration and right to practise. ## 10. Documents Required to Study Law in France

universities.name: The university and admissions route determine the final document checklist. Applicants commonly need
Secondary school certificate for undergraduate admission.
universities.desc: Bachelor's degree certificate for postgraduate admission. Official academic transcripts. Certified translations, where required. French or English language test results, if applicable. CV or résumé for postgraduate applications. Statement of purpose or motivation letter. Letters of recommendation, where requested. Research proposal for doctoral applications. Application form and supporting declarations. Proof of application fee payment, if applicable. After admission, international students may also need documents for a visa application, including proof of funds, accommodation details and other items specified by the relevant authorities. ## 11. FAQs About Studying Law in France Q1. Can international students study law in France? Yes. International students can apply to eligible undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral law programmes, provided they meet the academic, language and application requirements. Q2. Is an LLB available in France? The standard French undergraduate law degree is generally called the Licence en droit, which normally takes three years. It is not always labelled an LLB, so applicants should compare the qualification level, credits and recognition requirements. Q3. Can I study law in France in English? Yes. Some programmes, especially at postgraduate level, are taught in English. However, many undergraduate law degrees are taught in French. French proficiency may also be important for internships, employment and legal practice. Q4. How much does it cost to study law in France? Costs depend on the institution and fee status. For 2026–2027, the published standard registration rate at covered public institutions is €178 annually for a Licence and €255 for a Master's for EU/EEA/Swiss students. Standard differentiated rates for many non-EU students are €2,902 and €3,950 respectively, subject to exemptions and institutional rules. Q5. Can I become a lawyer in France after studying law? A law degree is an important academic step, but it does not automatically qualify a graduate to practise. Candidates must satisfy the applicable professional education, examination, training and other eligibility requirements. International qualifications and nationality can affect the route, so applicants should check the current official rules. How can Edu Hawk worldwide Consultancy help me study abroad? Edu Hawk worldwide can help students explore suitable universities, understand admission requirements, organise application documents, and plan their study-abroad journey. Students should verify academic, financial, immigration, and licensing requirements with the relevant official authorities.
